pull_requests.body:
## Motivation and Context

Implements the winner-logging decision in [RFC: Classifying allocations for per-subject experimentation opt-out](https://docs.google.com/document/d/153tRlj46l-XfBGCA2X_NvxW4vwYObaH8zm2moP_AqMk/edit), including **Handling holdouts using existing doLog**.

The agreed design reuses `doLog` for experimentation opt-out. Ordinary winners stop logging exposures; generated holdouts continue logging. Today, the retained experiment link keeps ordinary winners at `doLog=true`, so opted-out subjects skip them.

### PR stack order

**Position:** Stack A, first PR. Solid arrows show Git parent → child. The dashed arrow shows a deployment prerequisite, not a Git parent.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph A["Stack A: immediate opt-out compiler support"]
        W["#139368: winner logging (this PR)"] --> F["#139379: retain fallbacks"]
    end
    subgraph B["Stack B: stable activation metadata"]
        V["#139367: RC validation"] --> P["#139381: persist and publish"]
    end
    M["k8s-resources #12479: nullable storage"] -.-> P
```

| Stack goal | Review and merge order | Why stacked |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A: preserve ordinary delivery during immediate opt-out.** | [#139368](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/pull/139368) → [#139379](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/pull/139379) | Correct winner classification first. The fallback optimizer then uses that classification to retain skippable experiments' fallbacks. |
| **B: provide stable activation times for future-experiments-only mode.** | [#139367](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/pull/139367) → [#139381](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/pull/139381) | Separate schema acceptance from emission, so validators can deploy before producers. |

Both stacks start from `main` and can progress independently. [Migration #12479](https://github.com/ddoghq/k8s-resources/pull/12479) targets `k8s-resources/master`. Deploy it and RC validation before #139381; merging alone is insufficient.

## Description

- Read standard experiment lifecycle state in the compiler's existing database snapshot.
- Stop ordinary winner exposures after `ROLLOUT_COMPLETE` or `CODE_REMOVED`, without removing the experiment link.
- Keep generated holdout exposures, serial IDs, assignments, and analysis inclusion unchanged. Canary and bandit logging remain unchanged.
- Preserve logging when lifecycle state is missing. Use one organization-scoped bulk query.

After winner selection, the compiler keeps the two purposes separate:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    C["Completed standard experiment; experiment link retained"] --> W["Ordinary winner allocation: doLog = false"]
    C --> H["Generated holdout allocation, when applicable: doLog = true"]
    W --> D["Winner remains available to opted-out subjects"]
    H --> A["Existing holdout exposures and analysis continue"]
```

This changes exposure logging, not evaluation telemetry.

### Later stacks: preview

These are planned follow-up groups, not additional published PRs in this series.

| Order | Goal | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **C: complete activation coverage** | Establish usable activation metadata for supported allocation types. | Remaining lifecycle writers, canary/bandit coverage where supported, holdout timing, and missing-metadata behavior. |
| **D: shared fixtures and evaluators** | Apply the same cutoff rule locally and at the edge. | Timestamp fixtures first; Go/Rust evaluators, JSON/archive compatibility, Precompute transport, and cache handling. |
| **E: SDK delivery** | Let customers select future-experiments-only behavior consistently. | Extend existing opt-out integrations, pass the customer cutoff, and test request acknowledgement and cached-state compatibility. |

The existing immediate-mode SDK work does not wait for C–E. Future-mode enablement requires completed producer/consumer support and end-to-end validation; these five PRs do not enable it.

## How has this been tested?

The full UFC suite passed. Regression tests check 8,192 winner assignments and execute the holdout assignment query for both winners, global/selective holdouts, and primary/preliminary analysis. A negative control confirms that removing holdout exposures breaks primary analysis.

Repository snapshot and handler lifecycle tests compile, but local database setup is blocked by Docker storage errors. They still need a successful CI run. This is not deployed end-to-end proof.

## What is expected of reviewers?

Check that the implementation follows the RFC: only completed standard winners stop logging. Review snapshot consistency, organization scoping, and preservation of holdout metadata and the experiment link.

Evidence — 2. callers still send the deprecated field `ffe.experimentation.experiment.patch_lifecycle_deprecated{field:experiment_action}`, summed over the 30 days to 2026-10-21: us1 95, eu1 28, us5 17, us3 13. The handler counts each request before later checks can reject it (`experiment_handler.go:2259-2264`), and the metric records neither the action nor the outcome. So these are requests that set the field, not successful concludes.
Evidence — 3. opted-out subjects are randomized A probe on the #140422 evaluators, in immediate mode, with a `doLog=false` allocation that splits 50/50 between two variations before a fallback: 200 opted-out subjects got `a` 106 and `b` 94, and none reached the fallback. 🤖 **Comment from Claude working with Aaron Silverman:** **[P2]** Removing this flag from the compatibility payload matches the SemVer policy we want. Please make the policy hold when the optimizer prunes the SEMVER rule too. The policy we want: a flag whose authored allocations contain a `SEMVER_*` condition goes only to the tracer versions in `semverSafeUFCTargets`, whether or not opt-out applies. A flag with an override serves one variant and skips this check (`ufc/compiler.go:206-247`). Those versions isolate a `SEMVER_*` condition to its flag (`remote-config/direct_client.go:35-49`). Every other tracer gets the payload that `FilterSemverFlags` builds. With the org rollout off, server builds already apply the policy to the allocations before optimization (`ufc/compiler.go:247-259`). `FilterSemverFlags` checks the optimized allocations instead (`ufc/semver_filter.go:45-58`). So a SEMVER rule after an ordinary full-population allocation, such as a completed winner or a 100% rollout, is pruned, and the flag still reaches the other tracers. The pruned rule can never match, so this is about one consistent rule, not about a tracer parsing an unsupported condition. Before this PR, the same gap applied after any full-population allocation. Now it applies only after one with `doLog=false` (`ufc/optimizer.go:127`).
Evidence — compiled through BuildFlagsConfiguration - The test below compiles an ordinary full-population allocation, then a `SEMVER_GTE` rule, with server SemVer enabled. ## Motivation and Context

Implements activation metadata from [RFC: Classifying allocations for per-subject experimentation opt-out](https://docs.google.com/document/d/153tRlj46l-XfBGCA2X_NvxW4vwYObaH8zm2moP_AqMk/edit), **Opt-out after enrollment without new telemetry**.

The agreed contract preserves first activation through edits, ramps, pauses, and restarts of the same allocation. A new allocation receives its own timestamp when randomization starts. Draft creation and configuration rebuilds do not establish activation.

### PR stack order

**Position:** Stack B, second PR. Solid arrows show Git parent → child. The dashed arrow shows a deployment prerequisite, not a Git parent.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph A["Stack A: immediate opt-out compiler support"]

The fallback optimizer then uses that classification to retain skippable experiments' fallbacks. |
| **B: provide stable activation times for future-experiments-only mode.** | [#139367](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/pull/139367) → [#139381](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/pull/139381) | Separate schema acceptance from emission, so validators can deploy before producers. |

## Description

- Record `randomization_activated_at` atomically with standard experiment starts, including the generic exposure-schedule routes. Preserve the first value across later edits and repeated starts.
- Keep the value server-owned. Legacy replication omissions preserve known activation; senders that include activation state can explicitly clear it after allocation replacement. Existing running allocations remain unknown; no historical timestamp is invented.
- Emit optional `randomizationActivatedAt` in UFC JSON and protobuf. Preserve it through artifact decoding and include it in configuration identity.
- Give generated holdout allocations their own stable clock: the later of holdout creation and inclusion start. Covered winner selection does not reset it.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    D["New draft allocation: no activation timestamp"] --> A["First activation: store T in the start transaction"]
    A --> E["Edits, ramps, pauses, restarts: preserve T"]
    E --> R["Cross-DC replication: retain T"]
    R --> U["UFC JSON and protobuf: randomizationActivatedAt = T"]
    H["Generated holdout: use its own run's activation time"] --> U
```

This prepares metadata; it does not enable future-experiments-only evaluation. Canary and bandit activation writers, legacy-data policy, and Rust archive compatibility remain prerequisites for that mode.

### Later stacks: preview

These are planned follow-up groups, not additional published PRs in this series.

| Order | Goal | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **C: complete activation coverage** | Establish usable activation metadata for supported allocation types. | Remaining lifecycle writers, canary/bandit coverage where supported, holdout timing, and missing-metadata behavior. |
| **D: shared fixtures and evaluators** | Apply the same cutoff rule locally and at the edge. | Timestamp fixtures first; Go/Rust evaluators, JSON/archive compatibility, Precompute transport, and cache handling. |
| **E: SDK delivery** | Let customers select future-experiments-only behavior consistently. | Extend existing opt-out integrations, pass the customer cutoff, and test request acknowledgement and cached-state compatibility. |

The existing immediate-mode SDK work does not wait for C–E. Future-mode enablement requires completed producer/consumer support and end-to-end validation; these five PRs do not enable it.

## How has this been tested?

Database-backed repository, service, lifecycle, allocation-handler, and cross-DC suites pass against the migrated test image. Coverage includes both generic HTTP start routes, first activation, rollback, legacy replication, and explicit clearing.

Model, UFC, and orchestration suites also pass. No staging deployment was tested.

## What is expected of reviewers?

Review the implementation against the RFC: atomic first write, preservation across lifecycle changes, replication, and metadata propagation. Check that the derived holdout time represents the holdout run, not a covered experiment's winner selection. Keep future-experiments-only mode disabled until all producers and consumers support the field.

pull_requests.body:
## Motivation and Context

Apply the subject's experimentation preference before edge randomization. Support immediate exclusion and exclusion from future experiments without new telemetry or SDK preference history.

Design: [Customer-controlled telemetry and experimentation opt-out RFC](https://docs.google.com/document/d/153tRlj46l-XfBGCA2X_NvxW4vwYObaH8zm2moP_AqMk/edit).

## Description

The request selects a mode and supplies the customer-owned timestamp:

```json
{
  "evaluation_options": {
    "experimentation_opt_out_mode": "future_experiments_only"
  },
  "subject": {
    "targeting_key": "subject-123",
    "targeting_attributes": {
      "dd_experimentation_opt_out_at": "2026-10-01T12:00:00Z"
    }
  }
}
```

These fields are inside `data.attributes`. Modes are `disabled` (default), `immediate`, and `future_experiments_only`.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Mode + subject timestamp] --> B[Validate request]
  B --> C[Cached UFC]
  C --> D[Exclude allocations before targeting and sharding]
  D --> E[Assignments + policy acknowledgement]
```

- Immediate mode skips `doLog=true` allocations. Future mode preserves only allocations activated strictly before the cutoff. Missing activation skips the allocation.
- Continue later allocations without changing sharding or exposure behavior for eligible assignments.
- Reject invalid timestamps before origin access or response streaming. Preserve the existing boolean immediate-mode request and acknowledgement.
- Apply the same policy in Go, Rust JSON, and Rust archived evaluation. Buffered and streaming responses acknowledge the applied policy.
- Pin [fixture PR #52](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/pull/52) at `1c831fed02a428a1b0a4ac412da9b773e22df257`. The newer fixtures also require extended-version support in Go and malformed-regex flag isolation in Go and Rust.

### Dependencies

This PR targets `main`; it does not include compiler or database changes.

| Dependency | Required before |
| --- | --- |
| [Fixtures #52](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/pull/52) | Landing: merge and replace the candidate pin with the merged revision. |
| [Winner logging #139368](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/pull/139368), [fallback preservation #139379](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/pull/139379) | Customer enablement: retain ordinary delivery after exclusion. |
| [Activation metadata #139381](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/pull/139381) and backfill | Future-mode enablement: identify older allocations. |
| Future-mode SDK support | Client enablement: forward the mode and validate its acknowledgement. Immediate-mode client drafts remain compatible. |

## How has this been tested?

Canonical `bzl` suites pass for Go, Rust, and the Fastly handler. Shared fixtures cover 26 immediate and 42 future-mode cases. Rust checks JSON and archived results. Additional tests preserve assignments and exposure metadata for 100 subjects.

Fastly WASM tests cover both encodings and delivery paths, legacy requests, malformed input before origin access, acknowledgements, and activation timestamps outside nanosecond-range dates. Existing manually ignored tests remain ignored. No staging deployment or mobile end-to-end validation was performed.

## What is expected of reviewers?

Review the request and acknowledgement contract, the activation cutoff boundary, and the fixture compatibility changes. Confirm the listed enablement dependencies before rollout.
